answers.answer: Redis is an in-memory key-value store and data structure server: a network server that keeps keys mapped to typed values (strings, lists, sets, hashes, sorted sets, streams and more) in RAM, optionally persisting to disk via RDB snapshots or the append only file. It is meant for real-time applications where an on-disk database is too slow for the request path: caching (with eviction policies and key expiration), session stores, queues and messaging (lists as job queues, sorted sets as priority queues, pub/sub, streams), and secondary indexing, full-text and vector similarity search (vector sets still beta). It is also described as a document and vector query engine.

answers.answer: The two are RDB snapshots and the append only file (AOF). RDB: serverCron checks configured save points and, when enough changes and seconds have passed, calls rdbSaveBackground, which forks a child (redisFork) that writes a point-in-time dump while the parent keeps serving. AOF: a command log; feedAppendOnlyFile appends each propagated write to a memory buffer and flushAppendOnlyFile writes it to disk in beforeSleep, before replies are sent. The difference in durability (e.g. data lost since the last snapshot vs per-write logging) is not stated explicitly - the cost rows that would say so are withheld. Which one is used to restore data at startup when both are enabled: not stated.

answers.answer: The event loop (ae.c, aeMain) sleeps until file descriptors are ready and then processes their events, repeating until stopped. The connection layer's accept handler (connSocketAcceptHandler in socket.c) accepts a TCP connection and passes it to acceptCommonHandler, which creates a client; createClient installs readQueryFromClient as the read handler so the event loop calls it when bytes arrive. One turn: the loop wakes on readiness; read handlers fill query buffers and processInputBuffer parses complete commands and runs them via processCommand/call, which place replies in client output buffers; before sleeping again, beforeSleep flushes the AOF buffer (flushAppendOnlyFile) and calls handleClientsWithPendingWrites to send buffered replies, then the loop waits. serverCron runs periodic work such as checking save points. Further detail of a turn (e.g. timers ordering) is not stated.

answers.answer: The event loop calls readQueryFromClient when bytes arrive; it fills the client's query buffer and calls processInputBuffer, which chooses multibulk (input starting with *) or inline protocol, parses arguments, and calls processCommandAndResetClient once a full command is ready. processCommand looks up the command, checks ACL permissions, redirects keys owned by another cluster node, runs eviction when maxmemory is set, and refuses writes after a persistence error. Inside MULTI the command is queued and answered QUEUED; otherwise call runs the command's proc against memory. The reply is written with addReply into the output buffer. After a write, call hands it to alsoPropagate; propagateNow feeds it to feedAppendOnlyFile (AOF buffer, flushed to disk in beforeSleep before replies are sent) and replicationFeedSlaves (replication stream). beforeSleep then sends replies via handleClientsWithPendingWrites. Checks that can stop it: unknown command, ACL denial, cluster redirect, maxmemory/eviction (outcome not detailed), persistence error refusing writes; MULTI queues it instead of executing.

Why: the manifesto rejects making Redis threaded - threading is not a silver bullet and a single-threaded core keeps the design simple; scale comes from combining many shared-nothing single-threaded instances (e.g. Redis Cluster), which is simpler and suits NUMA systems. Extra threads: optional I/O threads (io-threads) read, parse and write sockets; background saves use a forked child (a process, not a thread). Costs/conditions: maintainers suggest enabling I/O threads only on machines with at least four cores and only when there is a real performance problem; threaded I/O is not supported for TLS connections; a single slow command delays every other client of the instance. repl-compression works only when io-threads > 1.
